name: Tyrone Ross AI operating stack
description: Layered inventory of the coding, model-routing and infrastructure stack, verified against live config files on 2026-09-07.

layers.name: Application / Interface
layers.definition: Where a request is typed. The human sits here; every layer to the right is reached through it.

layers.name: Tools
layers.definition: Capabilities the application calls on to do a job better: check a change, map a dependency, sharpen a prompt, review a design. Invoked, never in charge.

layers.name: Orchestration
layers.definition: Decides what work happens, in what order, and who owns it. Plans and routes; does not itself write code.

layers.name: Agent Memory
layers.definition: What every layer to the left reads at session start and writes at session end. Durable operating context, not storage.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.definition: What serves the models and hosts what gets built. Segmented into inference, database, middleware and app hosting.

segments.name: LLM / Inference
segments.definition: Serves the actual model. A tier or a named route resolves to exactly one of these.

segments.name: Database
segments.definition: Where application data and vectors live.

segments.name: Middleware
segments.definition: Queues, caches and the connective tissue between services.

segments.name: App hosting
segments.definition: Where what gets built is built, shipped and served.
